Chronic periodontitis

Adjunctive PBM may improve selected periodontal measures, but randomized studies also report no additional benefit over standard treatment.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

Adjunctive PBM may improve selected periodontal measures, but randomized studies also report no additional benefit over standard treatment.

Summary of the Evidence

The exact periodontium category contains 71 unique titles: 52 randomized human reports, four additional human nonrandomized or case reports, and 15 reviews or syntheses. There are no animal or laboratory studies indexed in this exact subcategory. Reviews overlap primary trials, and the title set includes different light-based approaches, so these counts do not represent 52 independent PBM cohorts. (Şengül et al. 2024)

Human and clinical evidence

Randomized trials examine adjunctive light therapy alongside scaling, root planing, or regenerative surgery. One trial separated a 626 nm LED PBM arm from photodynamic therapy and ozone arms after regenerative treatment; the reported clinical effects varied by outcome, and the trial’s primary attachment-level hypothesis was not supported. A systematic review of related PBM trials reported improvements in probing depth and attachment at selected follow-ups, but protocol variation and overlapping reviews temper confidence.

Animal evidence

No animal clinical or animal-model publication is indexed in the exact chronic-periodontitis category. Related preclinical work may appear under other periodontal categories and is not included in this count.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

No in-vitro or ex-vivo publication is listed in the exact category. Biomarker outcomes collected in human trials remain part of those clinical cohorts.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

Protocols vary. In the cited regenerative trial, the PBM arm used a 626 nm visible-red LED at 20 mW/cm² for 20 minutes at surgery and on postoperative days 1, 3, and 7, with 222 J total and 46.2 J/cm². The same trial also included separate antimicrobial photodynamic and ozone arms, so results must not be attributed to PBM alone when arms are combined.

Interpretation

Many reports exist, but the intervention label covers heterogeneous procedures and outcome measures. Evidence is more persuasive for selected short-term clinical parameters than for a uniform disease-modifying effect. Future trials should specify PBM dosimetry, isolate co-interventions, preregister outcomes, and use consistent follow-up for probing depth, attachment, bleeding, and patient-reported symptoms.

Evidence strength in source summaryLow to moderate for selected short-term pocket-depth and attachment measures
Publications and records71 unique titles in Oral > Periodontium > Chronic periodontitis.

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

The category contains 71 titles, including many randomized reports and reviews, but laser interventions range from PBM to antimicrobial photodynamic treatment and other diode procedures. Reviews overlap primary trials. Further work should isolate PBM from antimicrobial or surgical co-interventions and use consistent periodontal outcomes.
